steps: Welcome to the architect professional course: defensible decisions at Meridian. The C F O hands you two point four million dollars, and your decision record with service level gates must clear the board.
Next, the pilot holds four hundred and eighty thousand documents. Access control filters by role at retrieval, before anything reaches Claude, using hybrid dense, keyword and structured search.
Then costs run eight hundred and forty thousand dollars over budget. Prompt caching and routing between Haiku and Sonnet must cut forty percent, with service levels intact.
Next, the thirty-four tool claims agent drifts, so you decompose it into four subagents, turn on tool search, and put a human approval gate on payouts.
Then the chief compliance officer demands proof before patient health data flows: Enterprise, a B A A and zero data retention, since Pro and Team offer no B A A. The board approves.
Then three incidents hit with no trace I Ds, and an A B test turns out p-hacked. So you rebuild observability and evaluations, remembering that parity is not fairness.
Finally, the canary goes live at five percent of clinicians, on-call gets the runbooks, and any breach triggers an automatic rollback as it widens toward one hundred percent.
That is the whole rollout: every decision is on record, and the system is governed, observed and ready for production.
